docs.title: SpikeAgent
docs.text:
SpikeAgent is an AI-powered assistant for spike sorting and neural data analysis. It combines a Streamlit chat interface, SpikeInterface workflows, and vision-language-model curation tools to help laboratories move from raw electrophysiology recordings to curated spike trains.

The project provides two main ways to work:

  • Interactive analysis through the SpikeAgent web app.
  • Programmatic curation through Python APIs for VLM unit classification, merge analysis, and diagnostic plotting.

docs.title: Start Here
docs.text:
• Install SpikeAgent
  • Configure model provider API keys
  • Run with Docker
  • Use the interactive app
  • Run VLM curation programmatically

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Load electrophysiology recordings supported by SpikeInterface.
  • Guide preprocessing, spike sorting, visualization, curation, and merge workflows.
  • Generate diagnostic unit images for human or VLM inspection.
  • Classify units as good or bad using VLM-assisted curation.
  • Evaluate candidate merge groups for oversplit units.
  • Preserve human-in-the-loop review before final curation decisions.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: This document provides detailed documentation for SpikeAgent's programmatic API.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: SpikeAgent provides both a web interface and a Python API. This reference covers the Python API for programmatic usage, allowing you to integrate AI-powered curation and merging into your custom SpikeInterface workflows.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This section covers installing SpikeAgent for programmatic API usage in your own Python scripts and Jupyter notebooks.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or later
  • pip (Python package manager)
  • Git (to clone the repository)

docs.title: Installation Steps
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository: 

    git clone https://github.com/SpikeAgent/SpikeAgent.git
cd SpikeAgent

  2. Install in editable mode: 

    pip install -e .

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
# Test the import
from spikeagent.curation.vlm_curation import run_vlm_curation
from spikeagent.app.tool.utils import get_model
print("SpikeAgent installed successfully!")

docs.title: Core Curation & Analysis
docs.text: These functions represent the heart of SpikeAgent's AI logic.

docs.title: run_vlm_curation(model, sorting_analyzer, img_df, ...)
docs.text:
Classifies units as "Good" or "Bad" using a Vision-Language Model.

Parameters: - model: The VLM model instance (typically from get_model()). Note: gpt-4o is recommended for optimal speed. - sorting_analyzer (SortingAnalyzer): The SpikeInterface analyzer object. - img_df (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame of encoded images generated by create_unit_img_df(). - features (list): Modalities to analyze. Available: "waveform_single", "waveform_multi", "autocorr", "spike_locations", "amplitude_plot". - num_reviewers (int, default=1): Number of independent AI reviews per unit. Use 1 for maximum speed (default), or 3 for robust consensus voting. - with_metrics (bool, default=False): If True, includes quantitative quality metrics in the AI prompt. - metrics_list (list, optional): Specific metrics to include (e.g., ["snr", "isi_violations_ratio"]). See Quality Metrics below. - good_ids / bad_ids (list): Pre-labeled unit IDs for few-shot learning (provides visual examples to the AI). - unit_ids (list, optional): Subset of units to analyze. - num_workers (int, default=50): Number of parallel processes for API calls.

Returns: - pd.DataFrame: Results containing final classifications, quality scores, and detailed AI reasoning.

docs.title: run_vlm_merge(model, merge_unit_groups, img_df, ...)
docs.text:
Analyzes pairs or groups of units to determine if they should be merged.

Parameters: - model: The VLM model instance. Both gpt-4.1 and gpt-4o are highly effective for merge analysis. - merge_unit_groups (list): A list of unit groups (e.g., [[1, 5], [10, 12]]) to evaluate for merging. - Note: These are typically generated using spikeinterface.curation.compute_merge_unit_groups. - img_df (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame of encoded images generated by create_merge_img_df(). - features (list): Modalities to analyze. Available: "waveform_single", "waveform_multi", "crosscorrelograms", "spike_locations", "amplitude_plot". - good_merge_groups / bad_merge_groups (list): Example group indices for few-shot calibration. - num_workers (int, default=50): Number of parallel processes.

Returns: - pd.DataFrame: Results with "merge" or "not merge" decisions and reasoning.

docs.title: Plotting & Image Generation
docs.text: These functions prepare the visual data required for VLM analysis or human review.

docs.title: Encoding for VLM
docs.text:
Prerequisite: You must compute the required SpikeInterface extensions before generating images. To ensure compatibility with SpikeAgent's plotting functions, we recommend the following full suite computation:

extension_params = {
    "random_spikes": {"method": "uniform", "max_spikes_per_unit": 600},
    "waveforms": {"ms_before": 1.0, "ms_after": 2.0},
    "templates": {},
    "template_similarity": {},
    "spike_locations": {},
    "unit_locations": {},
    "isi_histograms": {"window_ms": 30, "bin_ms": 0.5, "method": "auto"},
    "correlograms": {"window_ms": 30, "bin_ms": 0.5, "method": "auto"},
    "spike_amplitudes": {},
    "noise_levels": {},
    "principal_components": {},
    "quality_metrics": {
        "metric_names": [
            "snr", "firing_rate", "isi_violation",
            "presence_ratio", "amplitude_cutoff", "amplitude_median", 'l_ratio', 'nearest_neighbor',
        ]
    }
}

for key, value in extension_params.items():
    extension = analyzer.get_extension(key)
    # Only compute if missing or parameters don't match
    if extension is None or not value.items() <= extension.params.items():
        analyzer.compute(key, **value)

docs.title: create_unit_img_df(sortinganalyzer, unit_ids=None, features=None, load_if_exists=True, save_folder=None, **kwargs)
docs.text:
Generates base64-encoded diagnostic images for individual units. The resulting DataFrame is used as input for run_vlm_curation.

Parameters: - sortinganalyzer (SortingAnalyzer): The SpikeInterface analyzer object containing the data. - unit_ids (list, optional): List of unit IDs to generate images for. If None, processes all units in the analyzer. - features (list, optional): List of feature plots to generate. Default is ["waveform_single", "waveform_multi", "autocorr", "spike_locations", "amplitude_plot"]. - load_if_exists (bool, default=True): If True and a cached CSV exists, loads it instead of regenerating. If False, deletes any existing cache and regenerates all images. If no file exists, always generates new images. - save_folder (str or Path, optional): Directory where unit_img.csv will be saved. If not provided, inferred from sortinganalyzer.folder. - **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments (currently unused).

Returns: - pd.DataFrame: DataFrame indexed by unit_id, with columns for each feature. Each cell contains a base64-encoded PNG image string.

Caching Behavior: - Automatically saves to/loads from unit_img.csv in the specified folder - If save_folder is not provided and analyzer has no folder, a warning is issued and images are not cached

docs.title: create_merge_img_df(sortinganalyzer, unit_groups, features=None, load_if_exists=True, save_folder=None, show_density=True, **kwargs)
docs.text:
Generates base64-encoded comparison images for unit merge candidates. Used as input for run_vlm_merge.

Parameters: - sortinganalyzer (SortingAnalyzer): The analyzer object containing the data. - unit_groups (list of lists): List of unit ID groups to evaluate for merging (e.g., [[1, 5], [10, 12]]). Typically generated using spikeinterface.curation.compute_merge_unit_groups. - features (list, optional): List of feature plots to generate for comparison. Default is ["waveform_single", "amplitude_plot", "crosscorrelograms"]. - load_if_exists (bool, default=True): Same behavior as create_unit_img_df. - save_folder (str or Path, optional): Directory where merge_img.csv will be saved. - show_density (bool, default=True): Reserved for future use (currently unused). - **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments (currently unused).

Returns: - pd.DataFrame: DataFrame indexed by group_id, with columns for each feature. Each cell contains a base64-encoded JPEG image string.

Caching Behavior: - Automatically saves to/loads from merge_img.csv - Each unit in a group is color-coded for visual comparison

docs.title: plot_units_with_features(sortinganalyzer, unit_ids=None, features=None, save=False, **kwargs)
docs.text:
Generates a multi-panel grid plot for each unit, displaying multiple diagnostic features side-by-side for human inspection.

Parameters: - sortinganalyzer (SortingAnalyzer): The analyzer object. - unit_ids (list, optional): List of unit IDs to plot. If None, plots the first 10 units. - features (list, optional): List of features to display. Default is ["waveform_single", "waveform_multi", "autocorr", "spike_locations", "amplitude_plot"]. - save (bool, default=False): If True, saves plots as JPEG files to [analyzer_folder]/feature_plot/. - **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments (currently unused).

Returns: - None (displays matplotlib figures)

Notes: - Creates horizontal strip plots with dynamically sized panels - Each unit gets its own figure with all requested features

docs.title: plot_units_with_features_df(sortinganalyzer, encoded_img_df, features=None, unit_ids=None, save=False, resize_height=None, save_dpi=300)
docs.text:
Displays the encoded images from a VLM DataFrame. Useful for visualizing exactly what images were sent to the AI during curation.

Parameters: - sortinganalyzer (SortingAnalyzer): The analyzer object. - encoded_img_df (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame of base64-encoded images (output from create_unit_img_df). - features (list, optional): Features to display. Default is UNIT_FEATURES. - unit_ids (list, optional): Subset of units to plot. If None, plots all units in the DataFrame. - save (bool, default=False): If True, saves PNG files to [analyzer_folder]/feature_plot/. - resize_height (int, optional): Height in pixels to resize images to. If None, uses native resolution. - save_dpi (int, default=300): DPI for saved images.

Returns: - None (displays matplotlib figures and optionally saves to disk)

docs.title: plot_spike_images_with_result(results_df, encoded_img_df, feature="waveform_single")
docs.text:
Plots curation results alongside unit images to visually verify AI classification. Separates units into "Good" and "Bad" grids.

Parameters: - results_df (pd.DataFrame): Results from run_vlm_curation containing final_classification and average_score columns. - encoded_img_df (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame of base64-encoded images (from create_unit_img_df). - feature (str, default="waveform_single"): Which feature image to display for each unit.

Returns: - None (displays two matplotlib figures: one for "Good" units, one for "Bad" units)

Notes: - Displays up to 5 units per row in a grid layout - Shows unit ID and quality score as subplot titles - Automatically handles dynamic grid sizing

docs.title: plot_merge_results(results_df, encoded_img_df)
docs.text:
Plots merge analysis results showing the comparison images and the AI's "merge" or "not merge" decision for each unit group.

Parameters: - results_df (pd.DataFrame): Results from run_vlm_merge containing merge_type and merge_units columns. - encoded_img_df (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame of base64-encoded merge images (from create_merge_img_df).

Returns: - None (displays matplotlib figures, one per merge group)

Notes: - Concatenates all features horizontally for each group - Shows group ID, unit IDs, and merge decision in the title - Each group gets its own figure

docs.title: get_model(model_name, temperature=0)
docs.text:
Initializes a chat model interface for use with curation functions.

Supported model_name strings: - OpenAI: "gpt-4o", "gpt-4.1", "gpt-5.2", "gpt-5-mini" - Anthropic: "claude_4_sonnet", "claude_4_opus", "claude_3_7_sonnet", "claude_4_5_sonnet", "claude_4_5_haiku", "claude_4_5_opus" - Gemini: "gemini-3-pro-preview", "gemini-3-flash-preview", "gemini-2.5-pro", "gemini-2.5-flash"

docs.title: 1. Automated Unit Curation
docs.text:
import spikeinterface.full as si
from spikeagent.app.tool.utils import get_model
from spikeagent.app.tool.si_custom import create_unit_img_df
from spikeagent.curation.vlm_curation import run_vlm_curation

# 1. Load data
analyzer = si.load_sorting_analyzer("my_analyzer.zarr")

# 2. Compute required extensions (using specific parameters for VLM)
extension_params = {
    "random_spikes": {"method": "uniform", "max_spikes_per_unit": 600},
    "waveforms": {"ms_before": 1.0, "ms_after": 2.0},
    "templates": {},
    "template_similarity": {},
    "spike_locations": {},
    "unit_locations": {},
    "isi_histograms": {"window_ms": 30, "bin_ms": 0.5, "method": "auto"},
    "correlograms": {"window_ms": 30, "bin_ms": 0.5, "method": "auto"},
    "spike_amplitudes": {},
    "noise_levels": {},
    "principal_components": {},
    "quality_metrics": {
        "metric_names": [
            "snr", "firing_rate", "isi_violation",
            "presence_ratio", "amplitude_cutoff", "amplitude_median", 'l_ratio', 'nearest_neighbor',
        ]
    }
}
for key, value in extension_params.items():
    extension = analyzer.get_extension(key)
    if extension is None or not value.items() <= extension.params.items():
        analyzer.compute(key, **value)

# 3. Encode images (Modality: Waveform + Autocorr + Locations)
features = ["waveform_single", "autocorr", "spike_locations"]
img_df = create_unit_img_df(analyzer, features=features, load_if_exists=True)

# 4. Run AI Curation (Fast mode with 1 reviewer)
model = get_model("gpt-4o")
results = run_vlm_curation(
    model=model,
    sorting_analyzer=analyzer,
    img_df=img_df,
    features=features,
    num_reviewers=1,
    with_metrics=True
)

# 5. Filter for good units
good_unit_ids = results[results['final_classification'] == 'Good'].index.tolist()
print(f"Found {len(good_unit_ids)} high-quality units.")

docs.title: Modality Features
docs.text: Feature Name Description Used In waveform_single Single-channel average waveform plot Curation & Merge waveform_multi Multi-channel template plot Curation & Merge autocorr Autocorrelogram of spike times Curation crosscorrelograms Cross-correlogram between units Merge spike_locations Spatial spike location scatter plot Curation & Merge amplitude_plot Amplitude distribution over time Curation & Merge

docs.title: Quality Metrics
docs.text: Available for use in run_vlm_curation(metrics_list=...): - snr: Signal-to-Noise Ratio. - isi_violations_ratio: Inter-Spike Interval violation rate (contamination rate). - presence_ratio: Fraction of recording where spikes are present. - amplitude_cutoff: Estimate of missed spikes due to thresholding. - l_ratio: Cluster isolation based on Mahalanobis distance. - nn_hit_rate: Nearest-neighbor true positive rate. - nn_miss_rate: Nearest-neighbor false negative rate.

docs.title: Data Availability
docs.text: This repository contains SpikeAgent source code. Large raw electrophysiology recordings, generated benchmark artifacts, and source data for manuscript analyses are not stored directly in Git.

docs.title: Public Data
docs.text:
Known public datasets include:

  • Neuropixels 2.0 chronic recordings in mice: https://doi.org/10.5522/04/24411841. The UCL Research Data Repository includes the AL031 and AL036 recordings used for the Neuropixels analyses and few-shot generalizability experiments.
  • Flexible-probe recordings generated in this study: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22180105.

docs.title: Simulated Data
docs.text: The MEArec simulated ground-truth datasets used for the 1-hour and 20-minute drift benchmarks were generated using the simulation procedure described in the manuscript Methods. No separate generated-data deposit is specified.

docs.title: Pending Public Artifacts
docs.text:
The repository's data-availability plan identifies these pending public deposits:

  • Figure and table source data.

The authors currently consider the public GitHub repository sufficient for code availability; no separate code DOI archive is planned. This plan may change before publication.

The full repository data-availability inventory tracks the pending URLs and access statements.

docs.title: What Not To Commit
docs.text:
Do not commit:

  • Raw neural recordings.
  • Generated SpikeInterface analyzer folders.
  • Generated source-data archives.
  • Generated plots or VLM reasoning dumps.
  • API keys or .env files.

Use discipline-specific repositories, Zenodo, Figshare, Dryad, institutional repositories, or another stable public archive for large data and publication-critical artifacts.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: Some SpikeAgent workflows require external datasets and live LLM or VLM provider credentials. Live model calls may be nondeterministic and may incur API costs.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
Install for local development:

pip install -e ".[app,dev]"

Install docs dependencies:

python -m pip install -r docs/requirements.txt

docs.title: Key Runtime Dependencies
docs.text:
SpikeAgent targets Python 3.11 or later. Core dependencies include:

  • SpikeInterface and ProbeInterface for electrophysiology analysis.
  • LangChain and LangGraph for model and tool orchestration.
  • OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Gemini integrations.
  • Streamlit for the web app.
  • NumPy, SciPy, pandas, h5py, matplotlib, and Pillow for scientific data handling and plotting.

docs.title: Study Data
docs.text:
• Public Neuropixels 2.0 recordings, including AL031 and AL036: https://doi.org/10.5522/04/24411841.
  • Flexible-probe recordings generated in this study: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22180105.
  • MEArec simulated ground-truth datasets for the 1-hour and 20-minute drift benchmarks were generated using the procedure described in the manuscript Methods.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Run focused curation tests:

python -m pytest tests/curation

Run broader local checks when all dependencies are installed:

python -m pytest
python -m ruff check src tests
python -m black --check src tests
python -m mypy src

docs.title: Reproducibility Limits
docs.text:
• Live VLM calls can vary across model versions and sampling settings.
  • Some analyses require paid API usage.
  • Raw and generated electrophysiology datasets are intentionally not stored in Git.
  • Large outputs should be deposited in public data repositories and linked from the data availability page.

The repository reproducibility plan records the manuscript environment separately from the current package requirements.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to use SpikeAgent for spike sorting and neural data analysis.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: SpikeAgent is a web-based AI assistant that helps you: - Perform spike sorting on neural recordings - Curate and validate sorted units - Analyze spike sorting results using Vision-Language Models (VLM) - Merge units that belong to the same neuron

docs.title: 1. Launch SpikeAgent
docs.text: After installation with pip, start the app with command spikeagent and open http://localhost:8501 in your browser.

docs.title: 2. Select an AI Provider
docs.text: In the left sidebar, choose one of the available AI providers: - OpenAI (GPT) (Could use gpt-4.1 as a starting test) - Anthropic (Claude) - Google (Gemini)

docs.title: 3. Start a Conversation
docs.text: Type your question or request in the chat interface. SpikeAgent can help with: - Loading and preprocessing recordings - Running spike sorters - Curation workflows - Data analysis

docs.title: Loading Data
docs.text:
Ask SpikeAgent to load your neural recording:

Load my recording from /path/to/recording

SpikeAgent supports various formats including: - Intan .rhd files - Neuropixels data - Other formats supported by SpikeInterface

docs.title: Spike Sorting
docs.text:
Request spike sorting:

Run spike sorting on my recording using Kilosort4

SpikeAgent will: 1. Check if the required sorter is available 2. Configure sorting parameters 3. Run the sorting algorithm 4. Display results

docs.title: Curation
docs.text:
Use AI-assisted curation:

Curate the sorted units using VLM

This will: 1. Generate visualizations for each unit 2. Use Vision-Language Models to classify units 3. Filter out noise units 4. Create a curated sorting result

docs.title: Merge Analysis
docs.text:
Find and merge duplicate units:

Find units that should be merged

SpikeAgent will: 1. Identify potential merge candidates 2. Analyze visual features using VLM 3. Recommend merges 4. Apply merges if confirmed

docs.title: VLM Curation
docs.text: Vision-Language Models can classify units as "Good" or "Bad" based on: - Waveform shapes - Autocorrelograms - Spike locations - Amplitude distributions - Quality metrics

docs.title: VLM Merge Analysis
docs.text: AI can determine if units should be merged by analyzing: - Cross-correlograms - Waveform similarity - Spatial locations - Amplitude distributions

docs.title: Tips and Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Start with small datasets: Test workflows on small recordings first
  2. Save frequently: SpikeAgent can save intermediate results
  3. Review VLM decisions: Always review AI classifications before finalizing
  4. Use appropriate sorters: Some sorters require GPU support
  5. Check quality metrics: Review quantitative metrics alongside visual analysis

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
"No recording loaded" - Ensure your data path is correct - Check that the file format is supported

"Sorter not found" - Verify the sorter is installed - For GPU sorters, ensure you're using the GPU Docker image

"VLM analysis failed" - Check your API keys are valid - Verify you have API credits/quota remaining

"Memory errors" - Reduce the size of your recording - Use a machine with more RAM - Consider processing in chunks

docs.title: VLM Curation and Merging Guide
docs.text: This guide provides an in-depth explanation of how Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are used in SpikeAgent for automated unit curation and merging, including how to customize prompts and behavior.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• Architecture Overview
  • VLM Curation
  • VLM Merge Analysis
  • Prompt System
  • Customizing Prompts
  • Best Practices

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: SpikeAgent uses an Ensemble of Experts approach where: 1. Feature Experts: Specialized AI reviewers analyze individual modalities (waveforms, locations, etc.) 2. Head Reviewer: Aggregates expert reports and makes final classification decisions 3. Consensus Voting: Multiple independent reviews can be combined for robust decisions

docs.title: Key Components
docs.text:
• Image Encoding: Neural data features are rendered as diagnostic plots and encoded as base64 images
  • Asynchronous Processing: Multiple units are processed in parallel using asyncio for efficiency
  • Few-Shot Learning: Optional example units can guide the AI's decision-making
  • Quality Metrics Integration: Quantitative metrics can augment visual analysis

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: Unit curation classifies each sorted unit as "Good" (well-isolated neuron) or "Bad" (noise/artifact).

docs.title: Workflow:
docs.text:
1. Image Generation: For each unit, diagnostic images are generated:
  2. waveform_single: Average waveform on peak channel
  3. waveform_multi: Multi-channel template view
  4. autocorr: Autocorrelogram (ISI distribution)
  5. spike_locations: Spatial scatter plot

  6. amplitude_plot: Amplitude over time

  7. Expert Analysis: Each modality is sent to a specialized prompt: 

    User → Image → [Waveform Expert] → Analysis
             → [Autocorr Expert] → Analysis
             → [Location Expert] → Analysis
             ...

  8. Head Aggregation: All expert analyses are combined: 

    [Head Reviewer] receives:
- Waveform Expert Report
- Autocorr Expert Report
- Location Expert Report
(+ optional quality metrics)

→ Final Decision: Good/Bad + Quality Score (0.0-1.0)

  9. Consensus (Optional): Multiple independent reviewers repeat steps 2-3, and results are combined by majority vote.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• num_reviewers (default=1): Number of independent reviews per unit. Use 1 (default) for speed, 3 for robustness.
  • with_metrics (default=False): Include quantitative quality metrics in the prompt.
  • metrics_list: Specific metrics to include (e.g., ["snr", "isi_violations_ratio"]).
  • good_ids / bad_ids: Example unit IDs for few-shot learning.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: Merge analysis determines if two or more units should be merged because they likely represent the same neuron.

docs.title: Workflow:
docs.text:
1. Candidate Identification: Use SpikeInterface's compute_merge_unit_groups() to find similar units based on template similarity.

  2. Comparison Images: For each candidate group, generate overlaid comparison plots:

  3. waveform_single: Overlaid waveforms (color-coded by unit)
  4. crosscorrelograms: Cross-correlation between units

  5. amplitude_plot: Amplitude distributions with histograms

  6. Expert Analysis: Each comparison modality is analyzed by a specialized prompt.

  7. Head Decision: The head reviewer determines:

  8. "merge": Units should be combined
  9. "not merge": Units are distinct neurons

docs.title: Decision Criteria
docs.text: The AI looks for: - Waveform similarity: Near-identical shapes suggest same neuron - Temporal relationship: Cross-correlograms show if units fire independently - Amplitude separation: Clear separation suggests distinct neurons - Spatial proximity: Similar locations support merging

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
Prompts are organized as plain text files:

src/spikeagent/curation/
├── vlm_curation/prompts/
│   ├── head.txt                    # Head reviewer prompt
│   ├── modality/                   # Feature expert prompts
│   │   ├── waveform_single.txt
│   │   ├── waveform_multi.txt
│   │   ├── autocorr.txt
│   │   ├── spike_locations.txt
│   │   └── amplitude_plot.txt
│   ├── metrics_header.txt          # Quality metrics header
│   ├── metrics/                    # Individual metric descriptions
│   │   ├── snr.txt
│   │   ├── isi_violations_ratio.txt
│   │   ├── presence_ratio.txt
│   │   └── ...
│   └── fewshot_instruction.txt     # Few-shot learning instructions
│
└── vlm_merge/prompts/
    ├── head.txt                    # Merge head reviewer prompt
    ├── modality/                   # Merge feature expert prompts
    │   ├── waveform_single.txt
    │   ├── crosscorrelograms.txt
    │   ├── amplitude_plot.txt
    │   └── ...
    └── fewshot_instruction.txt

docs.title: Prompt Loading
docs.text:
Prompts are loaded dynamically by prompt_loader.py:

# Curation prompts
from spikeagent.curation.vlm_curation.prompt_loader import load_all_prompts

prompts = load_all_prompts()
# Access: prompts["modality"]["waveform_single"]

# Merge prompts
from spikeagent.curation.vlm_merge.prompt_loader import load_all_prompts

docs.title: Step 1: Locate the Prompt File
docs.text: Navigate to the appropriate directory: - Curation modality prompts: src/spikeagent/curation/vlm_curation/prompts/modality/ - Curation head prompt: src/spikeagent/curation/vlm_curation/prompts/head.txt - Merge modality prompts: src/spikeagent/curation/vlm_merge/prompts/modality/ - Merge head prompt: src/spikeagent/curation/vlm_merge/prompts/head.txt

docs.title: Step 2: Edit the Prompt
docs.text:
Open the relevant .txt file in a text editor. For example, to modify the waveform expert for curation:

nano src/spikeagent/curation/vlm_curation/prompts/modality/waveform_single.txt

docs.title: Step 3: Understand the Prompt Structure
docs.text:
Each modality prompt typically contains: 1. Role definition: What the expert should focus on 2. Visual cues: What patterns indicate good/bad units 3. Decision criteria: Specific guidelines for classification

Example structure (waveform expert): 

You are an expert in analyzing neural spike waveforms.

Your task is to assess the quality of this unit based on its average waveform plot.

Good units typically show:
- Clean, stereotyped waveform shape
- Low noise/jitter
- Consistent amplitude

Bad units typically show:
- Noisy or irregular waveforms
- Artifacts or drift
- Very low amplitude

Provide your analysis focusing on waveform quality.

docs.title: Step 4: Test Your Changes
docs.text: After modifying a prompt: 1. Restart the SpikeAgent application (if running) 2. Run a small test dataset 3. Review AI decisions to ensure prompts are effective

docs.title: Tips for Effective Prompts
docs.text:
• Be specific: Clearly define what to look for
  • Use examples: Describe concrete patterns (e.g., "sharp peak followed by trough")
  • Set scope: Tell the expert to focus ONLY on their modality
  • Avoid jargon: Use clear, descriptive language
  • Test iteratively: Refine prompts based on AI performance

docs.title: 1. Choosing the Right Model
docs.text:
• For speed (default): Use gpt-4o with num_reviewers=1 for curation
  • For robust consensus: Use gpt-4.1 or gpt-4o with num_reviewers=3
  • For merge analysis: Both gpt-4.1 and gpt-4o are highly effective

docs.title: 2. Feature Selection
docs.text:
Curation essentials: - waveform_single + autocorr + spike_locations → Good baseline - Add amplitude_plot for drift detection - Add waveform_multi for probe geometry context

Merge essentials: - waveform_single + crosscorrelograms → Minimum viable set - Add amplitude_plot for temporal context

docs.title: 3. Quality Metrics Integration
docs.text:
Enable metrics for: - High-noise datasets: Quantitative SNR helps AI decisions - Strict curation: ISI violations provide objective contamination measure - Validation: Compare AI decisions against traditional thresholds

Recommended metrics: 

metrics_list = ["snr", "isi_violations_ratio", "presence_ratio"]

docs.title: 4. Few-Shot Learning
docs.text:
Provide examples when: - Working with unusual neuron types (e.g., very fast-spiking) - Dataset has specific artifacts - You want AI to match your personal curation style

How to use: 

# Manually label a few units
good_ids = [5, 12, 23]
bad_ids = [3, 8, 19]

results = run_vlm_curation(
    model=model,
    sorting_analyzer=analyzer,
    img_df=img_df,
    good_ids=good_ids,
    bad_ids=bad_ids,
    features=features
)

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
"Prompt file not found" - Check that you're editing files in the correct directory - Ensure filenames match exactly (case-sensitive)

"AI makes unexpected decisions" - Review prompt clarity - Add few-shot examples - Try different model (e.g., gpt-4.1 vs gpt-4o) - Check if images are rendering correctly (plot_units_with_features_df)

"Rate limit errors" - Reduce num_workers parameter - Add delays between batches - Use fewer reviewers (num_reviewers=1)

"Inconsistent results with multiple reviewers" - This is expected for borderline units - Review average_score to see confidence level - Consider using num_reviewers=5 for critical datasets

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
SpikeAgent exposes a small public convenience API from the top-level spikeagent package and more detailed functions in submodules.

from spikeagent import (
    create_merge_img_df,
    create_unit_img_df,
    get_model,
    plot_merge_results,
    plot_spike_images_with_result,
    plot_units_with_features,
    run_vlm_curation,
    run_vlm_merge,
)

Use the focused pages in this section for details on curation, plotting, and model selection.

docs.title: Supported Providers
docs.text:
get_model creates chat model wrappers for supported OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Gemini model names. Configure credentials through environment variables or a local .env file.

Python scripts and notebooks must load .env explicitly, for example with dotenv.load_dotenv(), before calling get_model.

docs.title: spikeagent.app.tool.si_custom.custom_plot.create_unit_img_df(sortinganalyzer, unit_ids=None, features=UNIT_FEATURES, load_if_exists=True, save_folder=None, **kwargs)
docs.text:
Creates a DataFrame of base64-encoded images for specified units and features.

This function can save the DataFrame to a CSV file for caching. The save path is determined by the save_folder argument or derived from the analyzer's folder.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default sortinganalyzer SortingAnalyzer

The analyzer object containing the data.

required unit_ids list

A list of unit IDs to generate images for. If None, all units are used.

None features list

A list of feature plots to generate.

UNIT_FEATURES load_if_exists bool

If True, and a cached CSV exists, it will be loaded instead of regenerating.

True save_folder str or Path

The folder where the 'unit_img.csv' file should be saved. If not provided, it will be inferred from sortinganalyzer.folder.

None **kwargs dict

Additional keyword arguments (not currently used).

{}

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

A DataFrame where the index is unit_id and columns are the requested features. Each cell contains a base64-encoded PNG image string.

docs.title: API Keys
docs.text:
SpikeAgent reads model-provider credentials from environment variables. The interactive app loads a local .env file. For local development, place it in the directory where you run SpikeAgent.

OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
GOOGLE_API_KEY=...

You need a key for the provider selected in the interactive app. The VLM examples use OpenAI vision models and require OPENAI_API_KEY.

For Python scripts or notebooks, load .env explicitly before calling get_model:

from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()

The VLM APIs accept a supplied model wrapper. It must support image inputs and structured output; compatibility depends on the selected model and provider.

docs.title: Custom OpenAI-Compatible Endpoint
docs.text:
If your lab or institution provides an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, set both:

OPENAI_API_KEY=your-institution-key
OPENAI_API_BASE=https://your-institution-endpoint.example/v1

docs.title: Safety
docs.text: Never commit .env files, API keys, raw recordings, generated model outputs, or large analyzer artifacts.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text: Docker is the easiest way to run SpikeAgent without managing all local Python and system dependencies.

docs.title: CPU Image
docs.text:
Create a .env file with at least one model-provider key, then run:

docker pull ghcr.io/spikeagent/spikeagent-cpu:latest
docker run --rm -p 8501:8501 --env-file .env ghcr.io/spikeagent/spikeagent-cpu:latest

Open:

http://localhost:8501

docs.title: Mount Data
docs.text:
Mount local data and result directories so the container can read recordings and save outputs:

docker run --rm -p 8501:8501 --env-file .env \
  -v /path/to/raw/data:/path/to/raw/data \
  -v /path/to/results:/path/to/results \
  ghcr.io/spikeagent/spikeagent-cpu:latest

docs.title: Helper Script
docs.text:
The repository includes run-spikeagent.sh:

./run-spikeagent.sh /path/to/raw/data /path/to/results

The script pulls the CPU image, starts the container, mounts provided paths, and opens the app. It includes a local build fallback for ARM64 when the registry has no matching image.

The helper stops and removes existing containers on port 8501 and may terminate a local process using that port. Use the direct docker run commands above when other services need to keep running on port 8501, mapping a free host port such as -p 8502:8501.

docs.title: GPU Image
docs.text:
For NVIDIA GPU workflows, build the GPU image locally:

docker build -f dockerfiles/Dockerfile.gpu -t spikeagent:gpu .
docker run --rm --gpus all -p 8501:8501 --env-file .env spikeagent:gpu

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: SpikeAgent supports Python 3.11 or later.

docs.title: Install From Source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/SpikeAgent/SpikeAgent.git
cd SpikeAgent
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e ".[app]"

On Windows, activate the environment with .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 in PowerShell.

For development, include the development tools:

pip install -e ".[app,dev]"

For documentation work only, install the documentation requirements:

python -m pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
python -m mkdocs serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/SpikeAgent/. If port 8000 is in use, run python -m mkdocs serve --dev-addr 127.0.0.1:8001 and use port 8001 instead.

If you also need the Python package, python -m pip install -e ".[docs]" installs SpikeAgent and its documentation extras together.

docs.title: Run The App
docs.text:
After installing the app extra, start SpikeAgent with:

spikeagent

or:

python -m spikeagent.app.main

Then open:

http://localhost:8501

docs.title: Optional Sorters
docs.text:
Spike sorters are not all bundled by default. Install only the sorters needed for your workflow:

pip install kilosort
pip install mountainsort4
pip install mountainsort5
pip install herdingspikes
pip install MEArec

Some sorters require additional system dependencies or GPU support.

docs.title: Verify Imports
docs.text:
from spikeagent import run_vlm_curation, run_vlm_merge, create_unit_img_df

print("SpikeAgent is installed.")

docs.title: VLM Curation And Merging Tutorial
docs.text: This tutorial demonstrates the programmatic VLM workflow for curation and merge analysis. The source notebook lives at tutorials/VLM_curation_and_merging_tutorial.ipynb.

docs.title: What The Tutorial Covers
docs.text:
1. Generate a synthetic ground-truth recording.
  2. Run MountainSort4 to create an initial sorting result.
  3. Compute the SpikeInterface analyzer extensions needed for visualization and metrics.
  4. Generate diagnostic images for each unit.
  5. Run VLM curation to classify units as Good or Bad.
  6. Find candidate merge groups.
  7. Run VLM merge analysis.
  8. Apply reviewed curation and merge decisions.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Install SpikeAgent and the sorter in an activated virtual environment:

python -m pip install -e .
python -m pip install mountainsort4

Configure OPENAI_API_KEY in the environment or a local .env file.

from dotenv import load_dotenv
import spikeinterface.full as si
from spikeagent import (
    create_merge_img_df,
    create_unit_img_df,
    get_model,
    plot_merge_results,
    plot_spike_images_with_result,
    plot_units_with_features,
    run_vlm_curation,
    run_vlm_merge,
)

load_dotenv()
si.set_global_job_kwargs(n_jobs=-1)

docs.title: Generate And Sort Test Data
docs.text:
rec0, gt_sorting0 = si.generate_ground_truth_recording(
    num_channels=50,
    durations=[30.0],
    seed=43,
    num_units=30,
)
rec0 = si.bandpass_filter(rec0, freq_min=300, freq_max=6000)

sorter_name = "mountainsort4"
sorting_folder = "./mountainsort4_sorting"
default_params = si.get_default_sorter_params(sorter_name)

sorting = si.run_sorter(
    sorter_name=sorter_name,
    recording=rec0,
    folder=sorting_folder,
    remove_existing_folder=False,
    **default_params,
)

docs.title: Create The SortingAnalyzer
docs.text:
analyzer_folder = sorting_folder + "/sorting_analyzer.zarr"
sorting_analyzer = si.create_sorting_analyzer(
    sorting=sorting,
    recording=rec0,
    format="zarr",
    folder=analyzer_folder,
    overwrite=False,
)

These examples preserve existing output folders. On a later run, use a new output path or load the saved sorting and analyzer instead of overwriting them.

Compute the extensions needed by the plotting and VLM workflows:

extension_params = {
    "random_spikes": {"method": "uniform", "max_spikes_per_unit": 600},
    "waveforms": {"ms_before": 1.0, "ms_after": 2.0},
    "templates": {},
    "template_similarity": {},
    "spike_locations": {},
    "unit_locations": {},
    "isi_histograms": {"window_ms": 30, "bin_ms": 0.5, "method": "auto"},
    "correlograms": {"window_ms": 30, "bin_ms": 0.5, "method": "auto"},
    "spike_amplitudes": {},
    "noise_levels": {},
    "principal_components": {},
    "quality_metrics": {
        "metric_names": [
            "snr",
            "firing_rate",
            "isi_violation",
            "presence_ratio",
            "amplitude_cutoff",
            "amplitude_median",
            "l_ratio",
            "nearest_neighbor",
        ]
    },
}

for key, value in extension_params.items():
    extension = sorting_analyzer.get_extension(key)
    if extension is None or not value.items() <= extension.params.items():
        sorting_analyzer.compute(key, **value)

docs.title: Run VLM Curation
docs.text:
features = [
    "waveform_single",
    "waveform_multi",
    "autocorr",
    "spike_locations",
    "amplitude_plot",
]

plot_units_with_features(
    sorting_analyzer,
    unit_ids=sorting_analyzer.unit_ids[:30],
    features=features,
)

unit_img_df = create_unit_img_df(
    sorting_analyzer,
    unit_ids=None,
    features=features,
    load_if_exists=False,
    save_folder=sorting_folder,
)

model = get_model("gpt-4o")
results_df = run_vlm_curation(
    model=model,
    sorting_analyzer=sorting_analyzer,
    img_df=unit_img_df,
    features=features,
    good_ids=[],
    bad_ids=[],
    with_metrics=True,
    metrics_list=["snr", "isi_violations_ratio", "nn_hit_rate", "l_ratio"],
)

plot_spike_images_with_result(results_df, unit_img_df, feature="waveform_single")

For few-shot classification, replace the empty good_ids and bad_ids lists with units that you have inspected and labeled from this sorting result.

Apply reviewed bad-unit removals:

bad_units = results_df.index[results_df["final_classification"] == "Bad"].tolist()
reviewed_bad_units = []
analyzer_curated = (
    sorting_analyzer.remove_units(remove_unit_ids=reviewed_bad_units)
    if reviewed_bad_units
    else sorting_analyzer
)

Populate reviewed_bad_units after inspecting the suggested bad_units, the reasoning, and the reviewer_*_class columns. Failed reviews are labeled Error in those columns and can be aggregated into a Bad final classification.

docs.title: Run VLM Merge Analysis
docs.text:
from spikeinterface.curation import compute_merge_unit_groups

potential_merge_groups = compute_merge_unit_groups(
    analyzer_curated,
    preset=None,
    resolve_graph=False,
    steps=["template_similarity"],
    steps_params={"template_similarity": {"template_diff_thresh": 0.3}},
)

merge_features = ["crosscorrelograms", "amplitude_plot", "waveform_single"]
merge_results_df = None
if potential_merge_groups:
    merge_img_df = create_merge_img_df(
        analyzer_curated,
        unit_groups=potential_merge_groups,
        features=merge_features,
        load_if_exists=False,
        save_folder=sorting_folder,
    )

    model = get_model("gpt-4.1")
    merge_results_df = run_vlm_merge(
        model=model,
        merge_unit_groups=potential_merge_groups,
        img_df=merge_img_df,
        features=merge_features,
    )

    plot_merge_results(merge_results_df, merge_img_df)
else:
    print("No candidate merge groups found.")

docs.title: Apply Reviewed Merges
docs.text:
from spikeinterface.curation.curation_tools import resolve_merging_graph

reviewed_merge_group_ids = []
merged_analyzer = analyzer_curated
if merge_results_df is not None and reviewed_merge_group_ids:
    merge_unit_pairs = [
        merge_results_df.loc[group_idx, "merge_units"]
        for group_idx in reviewed_merge_group_ids
    ]
    final_merge_groups = resolve_merging_graph(analyzer_curated.sorting, merge_unit_pairs)
    if final_merge_groups:
        merged_analyzer = analyzer_curated.merge_units(
            merge_unit_groups=final_merge_groups,
            sparsity_overlap=0,
        )

Populate reviewed_merge_group_ids only with result rows you have reviewed and approved for merging. With no approved groups, the analyzer is left unchanged.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Live VLM calls require provider credentials and may incur cost.
  • Model outputs can vary across model versions and runs.
  • Review curation and merge recommendations before applying them to final results.

docs.title: Spike Sorting Workflow
docs.text: SpikeAgent guides users through a SpikeInterface-based spike sorting workflow from recordings to curated sorting results.

docs.title: Typical Flow
docs.text:
1. Load a recording from disk.
  2. Inspect recording metadata and signal quality.
  3. Apply preprocessing such as filtering and referencing.
  4. Run a spike sorter.
  5. Compute analyzer extensions for waveforms, metrics, correlograms, amplitudes, and locations.
  6. Review diagnostic plots.
  7. Apply curation and merge decisions.
  8. Save final results.

docs.title: Interactive App
docs.text:
In the Streamlit app, describe the workflow in plain language:

Load my recording from /path/to/recording and inspect it for spike sorting.

SpikeAgent uses tool-guided responses to suggest code, run analysis steps, render plots, and ask for confirmation before high-impact workflow transitions.

docs.title: Programmatic Workflows
docs.text: Programmatic workflows should build around SpikeInterface objects such as recordings, sortings, and sorting analyzers. The VLM APIs expect diagnostic images and relevant analyzer extensions to already exist.

docs.title: VLM Curation
docs.text: VLM curation classifies sorted units as Good or Bad by analyzing diagnostic unit plots and optional quality metrics.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• A SpikeInterface SortingAnalyzer.
  • A DataFrame of base64-encoded unit images from create_unit_img_df.
  • A vision-capable chat model from get_model.
  • Optional few-shot example unit IDs.
  • Optional quality metrics such as snr, isi_violations_ratio, and l_ratio.

The example requires templates, correlograms, spike_locations, and quality_metrics to be computed on the analyzer first.

docs.title: Minimal Example
docs.text:
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from spikeagent import create_unit_img_df, get_model, run_vlm_curation

load_dotenv()
features = ["waveform_single", "autocorr", "spike_locations"]
img_df = create_unit_img_df(
    sorting_analyzer, features=features, load_if_exists=False
)

model = get_model("gpt-4o")
results = run_vlm_curation(
    model=model,
    sorting_analyzer=sorting_analyzer,
    img_df=img_df,
    features=features,
    with_metrics=True,
    metrics_list=["snr", "isi_violations_ratio", "l_ratio"],
)

print(results[["final_classification", "average_score", "combined_reasoning"]])

docs.title: Human Review
docs.text:
VLM outputs should be reviewed before applying final curation. The result DataFrame includes classifications, scores, and reasoning to support that review.

Inspect the reviewer_*_class columns for failed reviews labeled Error; the current aggregation can classify these units as Bad. Keep those units for manual review or retry the failed calls before deciding which units to remove.

After reviewing the results, set the unit IDs to remove explicitly:

reviewed_bad_unit_ids = []
curated_analyzer = (
    sorting_analyzer.remove_units(remove_unit_ids=reviewed_bad_unit_ids)
    if reviewed_bad_unit_ids
    else sorting_analyzer
)

docs.title: VLM Merge Analysis
docs.text: VLM merge analysis evaluates candidate groups of units that may represent the same neuron.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• A curated or partially curated SortingAnalyzer.
  • Candidate merge groups, often generated with spikeinterface.curation.compute_merge_unit_groups.
  • A DataFrame of base64-encoded comparison images from create_merge_img_df.
  • A vision-capable chat model from get_model.

docs.title: Minimal Example
docs.text:
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from spikeinterface.curation import compute_merge_unit_groups
from spikeagent import create_merge_img_df, get_model, run_vlm_merge

load_dotenv()
merge_groups = compute_merge_unit_groups(
    sorting_analyzer,
    preset=None,
    resolve_graph=False,
    steps=["template_similarity"],
    steps_params={"template_similarity": {"template_diff_thresh": 0.3}},
)

features = ["crosscorrelograms", "amplitude_plot", "waveform_single"]
if merge_groups:
    img_df = create_merge_img_df(
        sorting_analyzer,
        unit_groups=merge_groups,
        features=features,
        load_if_exists=False,
    )

    model = get_model("gpt-4.1")
    results = run_vlm_merge(
        model=model,
        merge_unit_groups=merge_groups,
        img_df=img_df,
        features=features,
    )
else:
    print("No candidate merge groups found.")

docs.title: Review Criteria
docs.text:
The VLM considers waveform similarity, cross-correlograms, amplitude distributions, and other visual evidence. Treat the output as a recommendation and apply merges only after review.

Compute the plotting extensions for the selected features first: correlograms, spike_amplitudes, and templates for this example. A cached image CSV may belong to an earlier candidate list, so this example regenerates the images.
